newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egypt to sell more shares in Arab Cotton.
newsitem.headline: Egypt to sell more shares in Arab Cotton.

text.p: The Egyptian state is to further reduce its stake in Arab Cotton Ginning by selling 100,000 or up to 300,000 shares to the public this month, an announcement published on Friday said.
The Holding Company for Cotton and International Trade said it was offering the shares in lots of 25. Individuals must buy at least 100 shares and funds and institutions at least 1,000.
The price would be fixed according to the share's closing price the previous day on the bourse and could be adjusted according to supply and demand, the announcement said.
The share closed up two at 60 pounds on Thursday.
The sale which opens on July 9 will further reduce the holding company's share of 37.35 percent. It had sold a total 52.65 percent of the ginnery to private investors last year.
The remaining ten percent is held by the worker's union.
The offer, conducted through brokers and National Bank of Egypt, closes at the end of the working day on July 10.
The company has paid-up capital of 11.21 million pounds among 2.24 million shares, or five pounds per share.
Arab Cotton paid a dividend of 2.1 pounds per share in the financial year ending on June 30, 1996 and expects to pay a 1.29 pound dividend for the 1997 financial year, the statement said.
After-tax profits are expected to be 4.39 million pounds in 1996/97, down from 6.95 million in 1995/96, the statement said.
